rationale:
Final iteration, so the goal is the most reliable design to race on the unseen track, not a new experiment. The best raced design is iteration 9 (score 432.15): sensors at x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05 with y = 0.07, sensor_size 0.012, kp 1.8, ki 0.5, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.2, last_direction. Iteration 9 finished the oval 20 of 20 at 1.88 s, with s-bend progress 0.68 and slalom progress 0.186.

The Evaluator's narrower-spread test (iteration 10, x = ±0.04) lost ground, scoring 260.62. Oval finish fell to 7 of 20, s-bend progress fell from 0.68 to 0.53, and slalom progress fell from 0.186 to 0.182. Its requested fallback applies: slalom and s-bend both fell below iteration 9, so the spread returns to ±0.05. Iteration 4 (±0.07) and iteration 6 (sensor_size 0.016) also hurt, so neither is reintroduced.

I considered untested tweaks such as kd 0.5 for s-bend oscillation (0.36) or kp 2.0. Neither has race evidence, and the unseen-track race is scored once with no later check, so I kept the proven design unchanged.

Expected result: roughly the iteration 9 profile, with the oval completing reliably and s-bend and slalom progress near 0.68 and 0.19 on the development tracks. The unseen track may differ. Measurements requested are the standard set so the outcome can be read against iteration 9.
